items.title: Smurfit Westrock (SW) Q2 Earnings Miss Estimates
items.summary: Smurfit Westrock (SW) delivered earnings and revenue surprises of -16.67% and +0.51%, respectively, for the quarter ended June 2026. Do the numbers hold clues to what lies ahead for the stock?

items.title: International Paper Pops for 2 Very Good Reasons
items.summary: Shares of  International Paper  which makes the containerboard used in cardboard boxes and other packaging, rose more than 5% Tuesday on two pieces of good news for the second largest containerboard producer in the U.S.  The first is a containerboard price increase of $80 a ton effective Sept. 1 that Truist analyst Michael Roxland wrote about in a Tuesday morning note.  International Paper  didn’t respond to Barron’s request for comment, but the report follows a similar increase of $140 a ton by rival  Packaging Corp  —also flagged by Truist—on Friday that sent paper stocks soaring.

items.title: JPMorgan upgrades International Paper as linerboard pricing cycle gains momentum
items.summary: Investing.com -- JPMorgan upgraded International Paper to "Overweight" from "Neutral," arguing that an improving U.S. linerboard pricing cycle and tightening supply-demand dynamics are likely to lift earnings across the corrugated packaging sector, with International Paper offering the most attractive risk-reward profile.

items.title: More producers announce price hikes for containerboard, boxboard
items.summary: Smurfit Westrock and International Paper announced containerboard price increases days after PCA’s, which is being called unprecedented. And boxboard producers announced increases for SBS and FBB.

items.title: International Paper Stock: Is the Turnaround Finally Worth Buying Into?
items.summary: The packaging giant is gaining market share and overhauling its operations, but a history of missed targets raises the stakes on its bet for a second-half recovery.

items.title: Smurfit Westrock to Report Q2 Earnings: What's in Store for the Stock?
items.summary: SW's Q2 results face mixed signals as stable packaging demand and pricing actions contend with lower volumes, cost pressures and uneven recovery.

items.title: Why Paper Stocks Were the S&P 500’s Top Performers Today
items.summary: Shares of paper stocks were the biggest gainers in the S&P 500 on Friday, following a report that prices for the containerboard they make that is used in shipping boxes and packaging were going up.  Truist analyst Michael Roxland wrote in a Friday note that  Packaging Corporation of America’s  plan to increase containerboard prices by $140 a ton in September will be positive not just for the Illinois-based firm, but also for rivals  International Paper  and  Smurfit Westrock  who he said are likely to follow suit.  Shares of all three stocks closed sharply higher, with International Paper up 11.2%, making it the best-performing stock in the S&P 500 for the day.

items.title: How Investors May Respond To Smurfit Westrock (SW) Lowered EPS Forecasts Despite Rising Revenue
items.summary: Smurfit Westrock recently faced lowered analyst earnings estimates for the June 2026 quarter, with consensus pointing to a year-over-year earnings decline despite higher revenues and an earnings report that has already passed. The company’s clean sweep of missing consensus EPS estimates across the last four quarters has become a central concern, intensifying uncertainty around how reliably it can convert revenue into profit.
